ev.q: CDC analyzed data from the National Immunization Survey Adult COVID Module
Asian and non-Hispanic White (White) adults had the highest ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage by the end of April 2021
to estimate the cumulative percentage of persons vaccinated by the end of each month
By the end of November 2021, national ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage was similar
Vaccination coverage among Hispanic and Asian adults was higher than coverage among White adults
In analyses stratified by Census region, urbanicity, age, annual household income, and health insurance
NIS-ACM is a random-digit–dialed cellular telephone survey of adults aged ≥18 years
disparities in COVID-19 vaccination coverage among minority racial and ethnic groups narrowed

methods_quotes.q: Differences in ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage were assessed by race and ethnicity
The Kaplan-Meier survival analysis procedure was used, with vaccination month as the time-to-event variable
T-tests were used to determine differences among groups, with p<0.05 considered statistically significant.
Data are weighted to represent the noninstitutionalized U.S. adult population and calibrated to state-level vaccine administration data reported to CDC.
Analyses were conducted using SAS (version 9.4; SAS Institute) and SUDAAN (version 11; RTI International).
